body:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1834205123 — Elevated 5xx / timeouts observed on Dedicated cluster us-west-2 (tenant=NovusRetail). Paging on-call.
sara_ops: paging @mike_oncall — we're seeing a sharp spike in 5xxs and gateway timeouts for NovusRetail. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/dedicated/us-west-2
mike_oncall: on it. can you paste the top metrics? 5xx rate, p95 latency, GPU util?
sara_ops: brief snapshot from 12:06 UTC:
- 5xx rate: 12.3% (baseline ~0.3%)
- 504 gateway timeouts: 420/min
- request p95: 3.8s (baseline 1.2s)
- node GPU mem utilization: 94% on pool-dedicated-3
- Kv cache hit ratio unchanged
taylor_sre: looks like a noisy neighbor — one tenant process is using most of GPU mem/compute. I can see NovusRetail pod set with big batch sizes and long seq lengths.
chun_eng: agree. logs show repeated OOM/eviction attempts and long kernel stalls. snippet:
```
2026-03-12T12:03:45Z NovusRetail-infer-0 stderr: RuntimeError: CUDA OOM
2026-03-12T12:04:02Z kubelet: Evicting pod NovusRetail-infer-0 due to memory pressure
2026-03-12T12:04:15Z router: 504 upstream read timeout to 10.0.7.23:8080
```
mike_oncall: confirming noisy neighbor on pool-dedicated-3. Which nodes are hit?
sara_ops: nodes: gw-node-23, gw-node-24, gw-node-25. GPU mem pinned by NovusRetail containers. Other tenants on same pool experiencing elevated latencies too (non-zero customer impact).
taylor_sre: Action plan — quick mitigations we can take right now:
1) Apply emergency per-tenant rate limit for NovusRetail at edge (reduce concurrency + batch size). command: `rctl tenant set-rate NovusRetail --concurrency 4 --batch-size 16`
2) Evict NovusRetail pods off shared pool to isolated maintenance pool for debugging: `kubectl -n prod annotate pod NovusRetail-infer-0 redwood/evict=true` and cordon node if needed.
3) Bring up emergency burst nodes (reserved capacity) in us-west-2: `infra scale pool-dedicated-3 --add 2-gpu-nodes --reason "incident 1834205123"`
4) Route NovusRetail traffic to dedicated fallback model variant (quantized) to reduce mem footprint.
mike_oncall: doing 1 and 4 now. reducing concurrency & swapping to quantized variant.
(chun_eng reacts :hammer_and_wrench:)
ellen_cs: looping in NovusRetail account team. Ellen: customer-facing note - Novus reporting timeouts in last 10 minutes. Can we confirm impact and ETA before I message them?
ellen_cs: sending short message to Novus: "We're aware of elevated errors and timeouts for your inference on us-west-2. We're actively mitigating and will post an update in ~15 minutes." (sent)
mike_oncall: concurrency limit applied. Observing immediate drop in GPU mem pressure on gw-node-23. 5xx rate went from 12% -> 6% in the last 90s.
taylor_sre: started eviction workflow to move pods to maintenance pool. NOTE: evicting will cause short additional errors — plan a controlled migration window.
mike_oncall: routing NovusRetail to quantized-4bit variant — backend responding faster, p95 down to 1.9s, 5xx down to 1.4%.
incident-bot: Deploy job job/evict-novus-1834205123 started by taylor_sre (job id 7843). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/7843
chun_eng: monitoring I/O and kernel preempt counters. If we see persistent instability after migration, we'll need to evict the tenant from the shared pool and review their batch tuning.
sara_ops: customer impact: NovusRetail production traffic experienced errors/timeouts from 12:02–12:12 UTC with degradation continuing until mitigations. Affected percent of their requests ~18% during spike window. Other tenants saw 2–6% latency increase but few 5xx.
mike_oncall: migration complete — Novus pods relocated to dedicated-maint-01. Post-migration metrics (12:20 UTC):
- Novus 5xx: 0.4%
- cluster 95th latency back to baseline 1.3s
- GPU mem on pool-dedicated-3 now 46%
taylor_sre: left a temp policy to prevent Novus from auto-scaling to high batch sizes: policy id policy-evict-1834205123. We'll follow up with Novus engineering to recommend queueing and batch config.
ellen_cs: follow-up note to customer: "We've migrated your inference workload to an isolated pool and applied temporary rate limits to stabilize. Please expect normal behavior. We'll coordinate a permanent tuning session to avoid recurrence." (sent)
mike_oncall: creating incident ticket INC-1834205123 with root cause hypothesis: NovusRetail requested high-concurrency, large batch inference causing GPU memory saturation and eviction storms; noisy neighbor effect on shared pool leading to elevated 5xx/timeouts. Tagging for postmortem.
chun_eng: adding next actions for postmortem: collect top-10 kernel logs, Novus request patterns (seq length/batch), autoscale config, and pool placement decisions.
sara_ops: handing off to @taylor_sre for night monitoring and postmortem. mike, will you stay for 15m to confirm stability?
mike_oncall: will monitor for 15m then handoff.
taylor_sre: acknowledged — taking incident lead. I'll notify next on-call at 00:00 UTC if unresolved and start postmortem doc in #eng-postmortems.
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1834205123 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Escalation: postmortem_required=true; severity=sev2.
mike_oncall: resolved for now. adding runbook note: consider per-tenant GPU reservations or stricter admission controls to prevent noisy neighbors.
sara_ops: thanks all — great coordination. Final summary will be posted to #incidents in 1 hour.
_message_preview: incident-bot: INCIDENT 1834205123 — Elevated 5xx / timeouts observed on Dedicated cluster us-west-2 (tenant=NovusRetail). Paging on-call.
